stem: Best guess: a small company collected $500,000 from customers this year. Receivables rose from $40,000 to $70,000. What was accrual-basis revenue?

choices.explanation: Rising receivables mean revenue exceeded collections, not the reverse.
That is cash-basis revenue.
This adds the whole ending balance without subtracting the beginning balance.

explanation: Accrual revenue = cash collected + ending AR − beginning AR = 500,000 + 70,000 − 40,000 = **530,000**.

stem: Which title is appropriate for a cash-basis operating statement?

choices.text: Income statement
choices.explanation: That title implies accrual GAAP.

choices.text: Statement of revenues collected and expenses paid
choices.explanation: Correct. The title signals the cash basis.

choices.text: Statement of comprehensive income
choices.explanation: A GAAP title that would mislead users.

choices.text: Statement of operations — GAAP
choices.explanation: The statements are not GAAP.

explanation: Special-purpose statements use titles that avoid implying GAAP; cash-basis operating statements are typically titled 'statement of revenues collected and expenses paid.'

stem: A company preparing income-tax-basis statements wrote off $12,000 of uncollectible accounts this year and estimates another $8,000 of current receivables will be uncollectible. What bad debt expense is reported?

choices.explanation: Correct. The tax basis uses the direct write-off method.
This adds an allowance-based estimate, which the tax basis does not use.
The estimate is not deductible until written off.
Actual write-offs are deductible.

explanation: Under the income tax basis, bad debts are deducted when specific accounts are written off (direct write-off method). The $8,000 estimate is not recorded.

stem: Which of the following is **not** a special purpose framework?

choices.text: Income tax basis
choices.explanation: A special purpose framework.

choices.text: Modified cash basis
choices.explanation: A special purpose framework.

choices.text: U.S. GAAP for private companies with PCC alternatives
choices.explanation: Correct. PCC alternatives are part of U.S. GAAP, a general purpose framework.

choices.text: A regulatory basis required by a state insurance commission
choices.explanation: A special purpose framework.

explanation: Special purpose frameworks include cash, modified cash, tax, regulatory, contractual, and other bases. Private-company GAAP alternatives are still GAAP.

stem: Cash paid for rent was $36,000. Prepaid rent was $6,000 at the beginning of the year and $9,000 at the end. What is accrual-basis rent expense?

choices.explanation: This adds the increase in prepaid rent; an increase means cash was paid ahead, so expense is lower.
That is cash-basis expense.
This subtracts the ending balance without adding the beginning.

explanation: Expense = cash paid + beginning prepaid (used this year) − ending prepaid (for next year) = 36,000 + 6,000 − 9,000 = **33,000**.

stem: A physician's cash receipts from patients were $620,000. Accounts receivable were $70,000 at the beginning and $55,000 at the end of the year; $4,000 of receivables were written off during the year. What is accrual-basis revenue (gross, before any allowance)?

choices.explanation: This subtracts the write-offs, but written-off amounts were billed revenue.
This ignores the write-offs, which reduced receivables without cash.
This reverses the receivable change.

explanation: Receivable roll-forward: beginning 70,000 + revenue − collections 620,000 − write-offs 4,000 = ending 55,000 → revenue = 55,000 + 620,000 + 4,000 − 70,000 = **609,000**.

stem: Which modification to the cash basis is generally considered to have substantial support under a modified cash basis?

choices.text: Recording revenue when services are performed
choices.explanation: Recognizing receivables broadly converts the statements to accrual, beyond a modification.

choices.text: Deferring rent expense arbitrarily to smooth income
choices.explanation: Arbitrary deferrals have no support.

choices.text: Recording estimated future warranty costs
choices.explanation: Estimated accruals are accrual-basis features, not typical modifications.

choices.text: Capitalizing equipment purchases and recording depreciation
choices.explanation: Correct. A common, well-supported modification.

explanation: Modifications with substantial support include capitalizing and depreciating long-lived assets, recording long-term debt, and accruing income taxes. Pervasive accruals would make it an accrual basis.

stem: In income-tax-basis financial statements, how is interest income on municipal bonds (exempt from federal tax) presented?

choices.text: Excluded entirely because it is not taxable
choices.explanation: Tax-basis statements present all revenues; nontaxable items are still reported.

choices.text: Included as revenue, often shown or disclosed as nontaxable
choices.explanation: Correct. Tax-basis statements include nontaxable revenues and nondeductible expenses, typically as separate line items or with disclosure, so the statements remain complete.

choices.text: Recorded directly in equity
choices.explanation: It is revenue of the period.

choices.text: Presented only in the notes
choices.explanation: It belongs in the statement of revenues and expenses.

explanation: Tax-basis statements include nontaxable revenues and nondeductible expenses, typically as separate line items or with disclosure, so the statements remain complete.

stem: Which disclosure is required in financial statements prepared using a special purpose framework?

choices.text: A reconciliation quantifying every difference from GAAP net income
choices.explanation: Differences must be described, but their effects need not be quantified.

choices.text: A statement that the statements comply with GAAP
choices.explanation: They do not comply with GAAP.

choices.text: A description of the basis of accounting and how it differs from GAAP
choices.explanation: Correct. Special-purpose statements describe the basis and the primary differences from GAAP (without quantifying), and include informative disclosures similar to GAAP where applicable.

choices.text: No disclosures are required
choices.explanation: Disclosures comparable to GAAP for similar items are expected.

explanation: Special-purpose statements describe the basis and the primary differences from GAAP (without quantifying), and include informative disclosures similar to GAAP where applicable.

stem: Cash paid for utilities was $24,000. Utilities payable was $3,000 at the beginning of the year and $1,000 at the end. What is accrual utilities expense?

choices.explanation: This reverses the effect of the decrease in payables.
That is the cash amount.
This adds only the ending payable.

explanation: Some of the 24,000 paid settled last year's 3,000 bill. Expense = 24,000 + ending payable 1,000 − beginning payable 3,000 = **22,000**.

stem: Which title is appropriate for the balance sheet of an entity reporting on the income tax basis?

choices.text: Balance sheet
choices.explanation: 'Balance sheet' implies GAAP; tax-basis titles must signal the basis.

choices.text: Statement of financial position
choices.explanation: Also a GAAP-style title without a basis qualifier.

choices.text: Statement of assets and liabilities arising from cash transactions
choices.explanation: That is a cash-basis title.

choices.text: Statement of assets, liabilities, and equity — income tax basis
choices.explanation: Correct. Titles should reflect the special purpose framework: 'Statement of assets, liabilities, and equity — income tax basis.'

explanation: Titles should reflect the special purpose framework: 'Statement of assets, liabilities, and equity — income tax basis.'

stem: A cash-basis entity received $48,000 in advance for a 12-month service contract on October 1. What revenue would be recognized for the calendar year under the accrual basis versus the cash basis?

choices.text: Accrual $12,000; cash $48,000
choices.explanation: Correct. Accrual: 48,000 × 3/12 = 12,000 earned; cash basis records the full receipt.

choices.text: Accrual $48,000; cash $12,000
choices.explanation: Reversed — the cash basis records what was received.
The cash basis recognizes all cash received.
Accrual recognizes only the 3 months earned.

explanation: Accrual: revenue earned Oct–Dec = 48,000 × 3/12 = **12,000**, with 36,000 unearned. Cash basis: all **48,000** received is revenue.

stem: Why might a closely held company choose income-tax-basis statements instead of GAAP?

choices.text: Tax-basis statements are required for all private companies
choices.explanation: No such requirement exists.

choices.text: Tax-basis statements eliminate the need for any disclosures
choices.explanation: Disclosures are still required.

choices.text: Its users (e.g., a lender and owners) accept the tax basis, which is cheaper to prepare and ties to the tax return
choices.explanation: Correct. Special purpose frameworks are appropriate when users agree to them.

choices.text: Tax-basis statements always report higher net income
choices.explanation: Tax basis may report higher or lower income depending on differences.

explanation: Special purpose frameworks are appropriate when users agree to them. The tax basis leverages records the company already keeps, reducing cost.
